extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing MPEP practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date of references (U.S. patents, U.S. application publications, and WIPO publications/national-stage documents) and for making provisional 102(e) rejections over copending applications. Includes treatment of international applications (pre- and post-AIPA), priority/benefit claims, and applicable form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application treated as a U.S. filing date for 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall have the effect for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 102(e) of an application filed in the United States only if (1) the international application was filed on or after November 29, 2000, (2) it designated the United States, and (3) it was published by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any one of these conditions is not met, the international filing date is not a U.S. filing date for prior art purposes under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). See examples and form paragraph 7.12 for application. (MPEP guidance and examples illustrate consequences.)

rubrics_metrics.name: If IA lacks U.S. designation or English publication: do not treat IA filing date as U.S. filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was filed on or after November 29, 2000 but did not designate the United States or was not published in English under PCT Article 21(2), do not treat the international filing date as a U.S. filing date for prior art purposes under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this situation do not apply the reference as of its international filing date, its date of completion of the 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) requirements, or any earlier filing date to which such an international application claims benefit or priority. The reference may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date, or 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as of any later U.S. filing date of an application that properly claimed the benefit of the international application (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIPA treatment for international applications filed prior to November 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application has an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, apply the reference under the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 374 prior to the AIPA amendments (pre-AIPA rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For U.S. patents issued from such IAs, apply the reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as of the earlier of the date of completion of 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit of the IA. WIPO and U.S. application publications resulting from such IAs never have a 102(e) date and are applied under 102(a) or (b) as of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) prior art dates for 35 U.S.C. 111(a) applications with no priority/benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For publications and patents of patent applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) with no claim for the benefit of, or priority to, a prior application, the prior art dates under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) are the earliest effective U.S. filing dates (i.e., the application's actual filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 111(a) application with no 119(e), 120, or 365(c) claims has its publication and patent accorded the application's actual filing date as the 102(e) prior art date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) for 111(a) applications claiming priority to prior U.S. provisional or nonprovisional
rubrics_metrics.description: For 111(a) applications that claim priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to a prior U.S. provisional or claim the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 of a prior nonprovisional, the prior art dates under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) are the earlier effective U.S. filing dates, assuming the earlier-filed application has proper support for the subject matter as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proper written support (see 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph) in the earlier-filed application when relying on its date. Examples illustrate dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(e) and foreign priority claims (35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or 365(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 111(a) application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) to a prior foreign-filed application (or under 365(a) to an international application) is accorded its U.S. filing date as its prior art date under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). No benefit of the foreign filing date is given under 102(e) for prior art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Hilmer and examples; foreign priority is not to be used to establish a 102(e) prior art date.

rubrics_metrics.name: All references of an IA filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 and published in English get IA filing date as 102(e) date
rubrics_metrics.description: All references, whether the WIPO publication, the U.S. patent application publication or the U.S. patent, of an international application filed on or after November 29, 2000, designated the U.S., and published in English under PCT Article 21(2) have the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date of the international filing date or earlier effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IA properly claims priority to an earlier-filed U.S. provisional or nonprovisional, the 102(e) date becomes that earlier U.S. filing date, provided the earlier-filed application has proper support for the relied-upon subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: IA filed on/after Nov 29,2000 but not published in English: no 102(e) date
rubrics_metrics.description: IA filed on or after November 29, 2000 but not published in English under PCT Article 21(2) have no 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date at all for their WIPO publication, U.S. application publication, or U.S. patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication dates, but never under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). If a later-filed U.S. application claims the benefit of the IA, the 102(e) date for the later-filed U.S. app's patent/publication will be the filing date of that later-filed U.S. application.

rubrics_metrics.name: IA filed prior to Nov 29,2000: U.S. patent gets 102(e) date at fulfillment of 371(c) requirements; publications do not
rubrics_metrics.description: For IAs filed prior to November 29, 2000, the reference U.S. patent issued from the IA has a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date equal to the date of fulfillment of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2) and (4); WIPO and U.S. application publications published from such IAs do not have any 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date and are applied under 102(a) or (b) as of their publication dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AIPA amendments are not applicable to IAs with international filing dates prior to November 29, 2000. If later-filed U.S. applications claim benefit, compute dates per examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation practice with respect to IA filing dates and language/publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. 111(a) application is a continuation of an international application (IA), the 102(e) prior art dates for the WIPO publication, U.S. publication, and U.S. patent depend on whether the IA was filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 and whether it was published in English under PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IA filed on/after Nov 29,2000, designated US, and published in English, the continuation's references have the IA filing date as the 102(e) date; if IA not published in English, the U.S. publication/patent of the continuation have the actual U.S. filing date as 102(e) date and the WIPO publication has no 102(e) date. Examples 7-9 illustrate permutations including pre-AIPA situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection over copending U.S. patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an earlier filed, copending, and unpublished U.S. patent application discloses subject matter which would anticipate the claims in a later-filed pending U.S. application with a different inventive entity, the examiner should determine whether a provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection of the later-filed application can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional 102(e) rejection may also be made if the earlier filed pending application has been published as redacted (37 CFR 1.217) and the subject matter relied upon is not supported in the redacted publication of the patent application. Use form paragraph 7.15.01 when making such a provisional rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions triggering provisional rejection when copending applications share an inventor or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: If (1) at least one common inventor exists between the applications or the applications are commonly assigned and (2) the effective filing dates are different, then a provisional rejection of the later-filed application should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisional rejection is appropriate where if the earlier-filed application is published or becomes a patent it would constitute actual prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102. Since the earlier-filed application is not published at time of rejection, the rejection must be made provisionally under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to overcome a provisional 102(e) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) can be overcome in the same manner that a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection can be overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may also be overcome by abandoning the applications and filing a new application containing the subject matter of both, or by showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor of this application, or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131. The rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.01 required language for provisional rejection (common assignee or inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.15.01 should be used to provisionally reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by a copending application having a common assignee or at least one common inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paragraph explains basis: earlier effective U.S. filing date of copending application would constitute prior art if published/patented, identifies possible rebuttals (derivation under 37 CFR 1.132, 1.131), and notes that terminal disclaimers do not overcome the rejection. Examiner notes specify use and related form paragraphs (e.g., 7.12 vs 7.12.01) to determine applicable 102(e) date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality prevents use of unpublished copending applications with no common inventor/assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee or common inventor and the application was not published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the confidential status of applications under 35 U.S.C. 122(a) must be maintained and no rejection can be made relying on the earlier-filed, unpublished application as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing dates are within 6 months (3 months for simple subject matter), interference may be proper. If the earlier application later issues as a patent, it may then be used as a reference in a 102(e) rejection against the still-pending application.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(f) rejection principle
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) bars issuance of a patent where an applicant did not invent the subject matter being claimed and sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must presume applicants are the proper inventors unless there is proof another made the invention and that applicant derived the invention from the true inventor. See MPEP §§ 2137–2137.02 for substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(g) rejection principle
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) bars issuance of a patent where another made the invention in the United States before applicant and had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section forms the basis for interference practice. See MPEP Chapter 2300 and §§ 2138–2138.06 for requirements and procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs (7.07–7.14 etc.) and statutory citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The specified form paragraphs (e.g., 7.07 Statement of Statutory Basis 35 U.S.C. 102; 7.08 102(a); 7.09 102(b); 7.10 102(c); 7.11 102(d); 7.12 102(e) including AIPA/2002 amendments; 7.12.01 pre-AIPA 102(e)) should be used in Office actions to make appropriate rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the particular part of the reference relied upon to support the rejection. Form paragraph 7.07 is required in first actions on the merits and final rejections; form paragraphs 7.07–7.14 are used only once per Office action. Follow examiner notes for appropriate selection (e.g., 7.12 vs 7.12.01 depending on IA filing date and chain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of priority/benefit claims when determining 102(e) date
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date, consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), U.S. nonprovisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 120 or 121, and international applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the relied-upon earlier-filed application's disclosure (and any intermediate application(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and 365(a) for establishing 102(e) dates. Ensure proper support in the chain of priority/benefit claims per statutory requirements (112/119/120).
